title: 2025-2026 AI/ML Research Fellow
description: Full details are available at: https://www.imachines.com/imi-ai-ml-fellowships-2025-2026-high-risk-research12 places will be opened for the 2025-2026 term, with a duration of 6 or 12 months at the applicant's option.The intent of the fellowship is to focus on high risk research: ambitious projects that may not produce results, but will have lasting impact if they work.We believe that publication in AI/ML has become overly biased towards short-term and iterative results, despite major gaps in our understanding of how to build optimal models.The goal of these fellowships is to give awardees uninterrupted time to focus on harder open problems, with adequate compute, talented peers, and weekly 1:1 mentorship from senior researchers but without chasing specific metrics.You will be expected to spend about 80% of your time on your own research, and up to 20% of your time either assisting other fellows or participating in wider research programs at IMI. We focus largely on applied research and its applications to online security problems, but often publish and support frontier research aligned with our broader interests. Serving hundreds of millions of people gives us a unique perspective as to what works at scale.Eligibility: prior fellows and research staff have come from disparate backgrounds, including early career researchers previously at MSR, FAIR, Mila, MPI, etc. and self taught mid career engineers transitioning into research. We do not discriminate on the basis of pedigree or age. If you have done interesting work, that is enough. You may reside anywhere in the world, excluding sanctioned jurisdictions. This will be a remote fellowship.Deliverables: we do not have hard targets, but generally try to get 1-2 papers with code done in a year, targeting NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, etc. At the end of your fellowship, if the threshold for publication at a conference or in a journal is unmet we will expect a final report, which may be published as a blog post.Applying: send a brief bio / CV link via this page. Include 1) the topic you are interested in working on, 2) a few lines on any relevant prior work you've done, 3) your github / scholar / x links, 4) your desired start date, duration, and other obligations (if any) during that period, and 5) a brief analysis of one of the projects outlined below.Each project intentionally includes some gaps or glosses. List the ones you see, and how you'd solve them. Alternatively, if you dislike the projects outlined under a particular topic, write up your own idea and why it is more promising, along with your estimate of time and compute required.Deadline: Admitting fellows in two cohorts. Deadlines for consideration: Oct 1 25, Feb 1 26. 3 week decision period. Rolling thereafter.Compensation: competitive location-adjusted stipend, conference and travel support for conferences with accepted papers.Selection criteria: novelty and importance, clarity of approach, feasibility given time/compute, alignment with topics. Panel review and one interview.Selection will be based solely on merit. IMI is an equal opportunity employer, and does not discriminate on the basis of age, disability, sex, orientation, race, religion or belief. We promote equality of opportunity for all, and welcome applications from anyone with talent, skills and potential.

one of the world’s most complex challenges: deploying robots in unstructured, previously unknown environments. description: Cybersecurity Architect – Global BankAbout The RoleWe are seeking a highly skilled Cybersecurity Architect to join our global banking organization. You will work at the intersection of technology, compliance, and risk, ensuring that our platforms and services remain secure, resilient, and trusted by millions of customers worldwide.As a Cybersecurity Architect, you will define security frameworks, guide engineering teams, and embed security-by-design principles across cloud, data, and application platforms. environments.Collaboration: Serve as a trusted advisor to engineering, operations, compliance, and executive teams on cybersecurity best practices and architecture decisions.Innovation: Evaluate and adopt cutting-edge technologies in encryption, secure networking, and AI-driven threat detection.What We’re Looking ForExperience: 8+ years of experience in cybersecurity architecture or engineering, ideally within financial services or other regulated industries.Technical Expertise: Strong knowledge of cloud security (AWS, Azure, GCP), SIEM/SOAR, IAM, firewalls, encryption, and secure application design.Regulatory Knowledge: Familiarity with global banking regulations and security frameworks (ISO 27001, NIST CSF, FFIEC, PCI, GDPR).Architecture Skills: Proven ability to design secure systems that balance business goals, usability, and compliance requirements.Communication: Strong ability to explain complex security concepts to technical and non-technical stakeholders, including transactions, and infrastructure. title: Cloud Infrastructure DevOps Engineer
description: Description: You will work in a highly critical production environment where your expertise in automation and systems engineering is essential. Supporting all three leading hyperscalers - AWS, Azure, and GCP, you will have a unique opportunity to develop and maintain solutions across multiple cloud platforms. In this role, you will leverage infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD pipelines, and container orchestration tools to ensure reliable, scalable, and secure cloud operations. Identify new market opportunities or potential pivots (e.g., carbon footprint reduction or AI-powered analytics).Leadership & Team ManagementBuilding a High-Performing Team: Hire, train, and develop talent across key areas like drone operation, data analytics, software development, marketing, and customer service. Early on, you may need to wear multiple hats or bring in versatile individuals.Company Culture: Cultivate a positive, innovative, and collaborative company culture. Lead by example and ensure open communication among teams.Employee Engagement: Foster an environment where team members are motivated, aligned with the company’s vision, and committed to its growth.Financial ManagementInvestment & Fundraising: Secure initial and future rounds of investment, potentially through venture capital, angel investors, or government grants. As the CEO, you will need to pitch the company’s potential, ROI, and scalability.Financial Planning: Oversee budgeting, financial forecasting, and cash flow management. Track key performance indicators (KPIs) and measure ROI on investments in technology and personnel.Cost Efficiency: As a startup, it’s crucial to find ways to keep costs low while delivering high-quality services. This includes negotiating contracts, evaluating costs of drone equipment, software, and other operational expenses.Marketing & BrandingBrand Identity: Define your company’s unique selling points and position in the market. Your branding should clearly communicate the value proposition of your drone services to farmers, agribusinesses, and other stakeholders.Customer Acquisition: Develop a marketing strategy to attract new clients in the agriculture sector. This might include digital marketing, partnerships with farming organizations, trade shows, and attending agricultural technology conferences.Sales Strategy: Oversee or manage sales teams, ensuring they have the tools and insights they need to sell drone services effectively. Develop a pipeline for new clients and work on building long-term relationships.Customer Retention: Establish strong customer relationships and maintain high service satisfaction. Offering support and continuous engagement with your customers can help build brand loyalty.Product/Service DevelopmentTechnology Integration: Ensure your drone service is equipped with the latest technology for agricultural analysis (e.g., NDVI sensors, multispectral cameras, AI for predictive analytics). The ability to provide actionable insights will be a key selling point for your service.Service Expansion: Depending on your market research, explore opportunities for expanding service offerings beyond crop monitoring, like precision planting, irrigation management, and drone-based spraying.Regulatory Compliance: In the US, drone services are regulated by the Civil Aviation Authority (FAA). Stay up-to-date with regulations and ensure that your drones and operations comply with all legal requirements.Testing & Optimization: Continually monitor and test your drones and their performance in real-world agricultural environments to ensure that the service you provide meets or exceeds customer expectations.Partnerships & NetworkingStrategic Partnerships: Identify and negotiate strategic partnerships with other players in the agriculture tech ecosystem—such as crop sensor providers, farm management software companies, and even agricultural co-ops or government bodies.Industry Relationships: Engage with agricultural leaders, innovators, and thought leaders to stay ahead of industry trends. Participate in industry-specific forums, panels, or working groups.Government Relations: In the UK, there may be opportunities for government funding for technology startups, especially those that help reduce environmental impact or improve productivity. Engage with government bodies to stay informed about grants or funding opportunities.Sales & Revenue GenerationRevenue Model: Decide on the appropriate pricing structure for your services. This might be pay-per-service, subscription models, or long-term contracts with large agribusinesses. You will also need to evaluate pricing for different types of crops, services, and scales of operations.Sales Channels: Develop sales channels that make it easy for farmers and businesses to access your services. This might include building a user-friendly app for drone bookings, offering bundled service packages, or targeting specific geographic areas.Scaling Revenue: Once you’ve validated the service model, focus on scaling it—both in terms of geographic reach and service offerings. At this stage, you’ll need to expand your drone fleet and potentially hire additional drone pilots or data scientists.Risk ManagementOperational Risk: There are numerous risks associated with running drone services, including crashes, malfunctions, or bad weather conditions. Develop contingency plans for these situations and ensure your team has insurance coverage.Financial Risk: Since investment is a key part of your business model, managing cash flow and ensuring you don’t run out of funds before reaching breakeven is vital. Having financial backup plans and contingency funds will be important.Regulatory Risk: Drone regulations are constantly evolving. You will need to stay ahead of any regulatory changes from the CAA and ensure the business is always compliant.Customer & Market ResearchMarket Analysis: Regularly conduct market research to identify new trends, customer needs, and competitors. Stay on top of technological advancements in agriculture to better serve your clients.Customer Feedback: Collect and analyze customer feedback to refine your offerings. Whether it’s through surveys or direct interactions, understanding your customer’s pain points will help improve the service you provide.Legal & ComplianceLegal Framework: Ensure all contracts, partnerships, and business operations comply with US laws, including intellectual property protections (patents for unique technology), labor laws, and privacy laws.Data Protection: Since drones will collect vast amounts of agricultural data, you’ll need to make sure that you comply with the US’s data protection laws, to protect sensitive customer information.Specific Challenges to Anticipate as a CEO in this Sector:Technology Reliability: In the early stages, drone technology may not be perfect, and ensuring reliability and uptime will be crucial.Public Perception: There can be concerns over drones flying over private property or noise pollution in rural areas. title: Vice President North America Projects
description: Job DescriptionPosition Title: Vice President, North America Projects Reports To: Regional CEO / Chief Operating Officer / Global Head of Projects (depending on company structure) Location: North America (New York, Toronto, Chicago, or other major financial hubs) Department: Strategy & Project Management Office (PMO) Employment Type: Full-Time, Executive LevelPosition OverviewThe Vice President, North America Projects, will play a critical leadership role in driving the successful execution of the firm’s most strategic initiatives across the North American region. This executive will be responsible for leading, managing, and delivering high-impact projects that align with the company’s growth strategy, operational excellence goals, and innovation agenda. Acting as a bridge between global leadership, regional business units, and external stakeholders, the VP will oversee projects in areas such as business expansion, regulatory adaptation, digital transformation, mergers and acquisitions, product development, and organizational integration.The role requires a strategic thinker with strong execution capabilities, a deep understanding of the North American financial services landscape, and proven experience in managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects within highly regulated environments. The successful candidate will demonstrate exceptional leadership, problem-solving, and communication skills while maintaining a sharp focus on results and sustainable business impact.Key Responsibilities1. Strategic Project LeadershipLead the design, planning, and execution of high-priority projects across the North American business portfolio.Translate corporate strategy into actionable project roadmaps, ensuring objectives are aligned with regional business goals and global priorities.Manage end-to-end project lifecycles, from initiation to delivery, including scoping, resource allocation, risk assessment, execution, and post-implementation review.Drive large-scale transformation programs in areas such as digitalization, operational efficiency, and customer experience enhancement.Provide project governance, oversight, and direction to ensure on-time, on-budget, and on-quality delivery.2. Business Development and Market ExpansionPartner with business heads to identify new opportunities in the North American market, including potential acquisitions, partnerships, and new product launches.Lead feasibility studies and business cases to support investment decisions.Develop and nurture strategic relationships with regulators, financial institutions, technology partners, and other ecosystem players.Ensure projects contribute to market competitiveness, client satisfaction, and sustainable revenue growth.3. Cross-Functional and International CollaborationCollaborate with headquarters and global business units to align North American initiatives with international strategies.Facilitate communication between regional offices, functional departments, and external stakeholders to eliminate silos and enhance project efficiency.Provide leadership and guidance to project teams, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and innovation.Act as a cultural bridge, ensuring effective communication and alignment between North American operations and the global organization.4. Risk and Compliance ManagementEnsure all projects adhere to North American financial regulations, compliance requirements, and corporate governance standards.Identify, assess, and mitigate project risks, establishing robust risk management frameworks.Proactively monitor regulatory and market developments in North America, adjusting project strategies as needed.Maintain the highest standards of ethics, compliance, and professional conduct in all project activities.5. Performance Measurement and ReportingDevelop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to track project progress and success.Provide regular updates and comprehensive reports to executive leadership, highlighting achievements, challenges, and corrective actions.Apply data-driven decision-making to enhance project outcomes and optimize resource utilization.Establish mechanisms for continuous improvement, capturing lessons learned and best practices for future projects.Qualifications and ExperienceEducationMaster’s degree in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or a related discipline required.MBA, CFA, or PMP certification strongly preferred.Professional ExperienceMinimum of 18+years of experience in the financial services industry, consulting, or project management within large-scale organizations.At least 5 years of leadership experience in managing complex, cross-border, or multi-stakeholder projects.Demonstrated track record of delivering strategic initiatives in areas such as mergers & acquisitions, digital transformation, or regulatory compliance.Strong familiarity with North American financial markets, regulatory frameworks, and competitive dynamics.Prior experience in a multinational financial institution or professional services firm is highly desirable.Technical and Functional CompetenciesAdvanced knowledge of financial products, capital markets, and operational processes.Proficiency in project management methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid) and tools.Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.Financial modeling and business case development expertise.Ability to manage budgets, timelines, and resources effectively.Leadership and Interpersonal SkillsExcellent leadership capabilities with proven ability to inspire and motivate teams.Outstanding communication and presentation skills, with fluency in English; proficiency in additional languages (Mandarin, French, or Spanish) is an asset.Strong stakeholder management and negotiation skills, with the ability to build trust across cultures and organizations.High level of emotional intelligence, resilience, and adaptability in fast-changing environments.Entrepreneurial mindset with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.Key Success FactorsAbility to bridge global strategy with local execution, ensuring alignment between corporate goals and North American market realities.Track record of driving measurable impact in terms of revenue growth, efficiency improvement, or risk mitigation.Strong reputation as a trusted advisor to senior executives and external partners.Demonstrated agility in navigating complex regulatory, cultural, and operational landscapes.Capacity to lead with integrity, innovation, and inclusivity.Opportunities and Challenges of the RoleThe Vice President, North America Projects, will join the company at a critical juncture as it expands its presence and influence in one of the world’s most competitive financial markets. Opportunities include shaping the firm’s growth trajectory in North America, spearheading digital and organizational transformation, and strengthening relationships with regulators and strategic partners.At the same time, the role comes with challenges inherent to the fast-paced, highly regulated, and competitive financial industry. The VP will need to balance global alignment with local realities, manage diverse stakeholder expectations, and deliver results under tight deadlines and complex regulatory scrutiny. Success will require strategic vision, operational excellence, and the ability to thrive in ambiguity.

title: Summer Associate Internship (Application Whitelisting Security Analyst)
description: OverviewTeam Overview:Application Whitelisting is a team within the Service Transition group of NFCU’s Enterprise Technology Services (ETS). The team manages policies, standards, and processes that govern the use of applications—from inception to retirement—within NFCU compute environments. "Applications" include executables, libraries, scripts, macros, browser plug-ins (or add-ons/extensions), configuration files, and application-related registry entries.The team’s primary responsibility is to review, enhance, and implement controls that ensure applications used within NFCU comply with key security policies and standards. A key outcome is the prevention of unauthorized or unvetted software execution on desktops and servers, reducing exposure to security vulnerabilities. This role offers exposure to enterprise security practices, application lifecycle management, and cross-functional collaboration with IT and security teams.Potential ProjectAs a Summer Associate, you may contribute to the following initiatives:Analyze and categorize application data from tools such as Microsoft Defender, Black Duck, and Checkmarx to identify inconsistencies and build a centralized whitelisting inventory.Design and automate reporting mechanisms for whitelisting status, risk scores, and ownership to improve visibility and decision-making.Collaborate with ServiceNow and CMDB teams to validate data ingestion, resolve discrepancies, and align with enterprise architecture standards.Support attestation workflows and governance discussions to ensure whitelisting policies align with enterprise standards and reduce risk exposure.Develop scripts and APIs to automate data integration and streamline inventory maintenance.Present findings, process improvements, and recommendations to leadership, contributing to the formalization of the whitelisting service.The Summer Associate Program is a 12-week internship running from May to August 2026. Interns will work on meaningful projects that contribute to NFCU’s mission while gaining hands-on experience in cybersecurity and enterprise technology.
